Release of bilbycast-edge version {{VERSION}}.

## Changes

{{CHANGES}}

## Upgrading from v0.116.0 or earlier

<!-- Static text: remove once no supported upgrade starts at v0.116.0 or earlier. -->
- **Upgrade every edge with an RTP input carrying `fec_decode` before any edge with an RTP output carrying `fec_encode`.** SMPTE 2022-1 FEC from an RTP output now protects the datagrams it sends; before this release it protected almost nothing outside a 2022-7 output forwarding RTP, so receivers rarely rebuilt a packet. An older single-leg receiver fed by an upgraded sender publishes each rebuilt packet as soon as it has it, after newer ones: continuity errors, and a PCR that steps back. An upgraded single-leg receiver publishes only repairs that are in order. A 2022-7 input without `path_differential_ms` publishes repairs as they come on any version, so give it one. An older sender feeding an upgraded receiver behaves as before. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#smpte-2022-1-fec-configuration).
- **FEC covers at most 8 columns and 8 rows.** The FEC header names a column or row in 3 bits, so an output configured with `columns` or `rows` above 8 sends no FEC for columns or rows from 8 up (a packet in both is unprotected) and logs a warning at start (except `columns: 1`, which sends no row FEC and so loses nothing). `columns: 1` now sends column FEC only. `8 x 8` is the largest shape every column and row of which is protected.
- **New Warning `egress_pcr_accuracy_exceeded` on UDP and RTP outputs that re-encode video.** Such an output stays on `forward` egress pacing under auto, so it sends packets as its encoder delivers them. Running outputs whose PCR send jitter (`pcr_trust` p99) is above 30 ms start raising this Warning a few minutes after the upgrade. On the test rig that was most video transcodes. Nothing changes on the wire. The message names `egress_pacing: "pcr"` as the fix and its latency cost: about 50 ms, rising to the longest encoder stall it absorbs. Switching restarts the output, and its encoder's open counts as such a stall — most of a second on some hardware encoders. Past about 1 s the egress residence cap sheds packets instead (`egress_shed`). A lighter encode keeps the latency down. An output pinned to `forward` raises it too, and can only acknowledge it. Check that the receiver copes with `pcr` pacing before relying on it. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#outputs-that-re-encode-video).
- **SRT socket-group bonding applies each member's source and weight.** Before this release `local_addr`, `interface_binding` and `weight` on bonding endpoints were accepted and ignored: every member left by the default route, and libsrt chose the backup-mode primary. Now each member binds its source, so a source that is not an address of this host (a typo, or a static IP the DHCP server or carrier has since changed), or one the network will not route, leaves that member unable to connect; if every member is like that, the bond does not connect at all. Check each pinned member before upgrading with `ip -br addr` and `ip route get <peer> from <source>`. In backup mode the lowest configured weight is now the primary. A member that breaks is re-added while another one carries, where before it stayed gone until every member had failed. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#native-libsrt-srt-bonding-socket-groups).
- **Creating or deleting a tunnel and `PUT /api/v1/ptp` need the `admin` role**, like every other write on `/api/v1`. With auth on, a `monitor` token is refused 403 (`admin role required`) there; releases up to 0.116.0 accepted any valid JWT on those three routes. A script that makes these calls with a `monitor` token needs an `admin` one. See [api-security.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/api-security.md).
- **HEVC CMAF outputs open one new init generation at their first start after the upgrade.** The `hvcC` an HEVC CMAF output writes, passthrough and `video_encode` alike, now reads its profile, level, chroma format and bit depths from the SPS; it took them from the wrong bytes, so a Main 10 level 4.1 source was described as profile byte 0x01, level 0, 8-bit. The changed init opens a new generation once: a running DVR stream shows one `#EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY` with a per-row `#EXT-X-MAP`, and a DVR clip straddling it is cut exactly from the recording, or refused where the exact cut falls back to whole segments. H.264 outputs are unaffected. See [cmaf.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/cmaf.md).
- **RTMP output: passthrough video and the FLV timeline change on the wire.** An HEVC source whose slices name more than one PPS now decodes at the receiver: the sequence header carries every parameter set the source has sent, and HEVC tags keep theirs in-band, the `hvcC` marking no array complete (`array_completeness` 0), as FFmpeg writes it. An H.264 intra picture carrying a recovery-point SEI (an IDR-less open-GOP source) is flagged a keyframe, with the sequence header re-sent ahead of it. Every tag goes through one timeline per connection, which continues across the 33-bit PTS wrap, loops and input switches instead of stepping back to 0, gives a picture with no PTS its predecessor's time, and re-anchors transcoded audio at each seam; `silent_fallback` silence now carries real timestamps rather than 0, and the AAC sequence header goes out with the first encoded frame, at its timestamp. A pause of a video-only source is kept up to 10 s, and an outage of both tracks past 3 s is closed. See [supported-protocols.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/supported-protocols.md#rtmprtmps).
- **RTMP output: re-encoded AAC goes out as raw access units, and an HE-AAC target's sequence header names its core.** Every AAC tag an `audio_encode` output re-encoded (`silent_fallback` silence included) used to carry the encoder's 7-byte ADTS header inside it; the same-codec fast path, which passes the source's frames through, was never affected. ffmpeg-family receivers read past it; GStreamer's faad (libfaad2) decoded nothing, and receivers that rebuild ADTS from the sequence header, the edge's own RTMP input among them, wrapped a second header around it. Each tag now carries the raw access unit, 7 bytes per frame less on `bytes_sent`: faad decodes it, the edge's RTMP input wraps it in one header, and ffmpeg decodes it as before. An `he_aac_v1` / `he_aac_v2` target's sequence header now names the core it carries, half the output rate (24 kHz for a 48 kHz output) and, for `he_aac_v2`, mono, with SBR / PS signalled implicitly, as passthrough of an HE-AAC source always announced it. It used to name the output rate and channels. A dashboard that reads only the sequence header now shows the core's rate and, for `he_aac_v2`, mono. ffmpeg (ffprobe included), GStreamer's faad and fdk-aac find SBR / PS in the stream and decode it at the configured rate and channels. See [supported-protocols.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/supported-protocols.md#rtmprtmps).
- **PCE-signalled AAC (channel configuration 0, ISDB-T 1seg) is published decodably on RTMP and CMAF and in MP4 exports.** Such a source names its channel layout in a program_config_element that only some frames carry. RTMP passthrough used to send a two-byte sequence header naming channel configuration 0 and no layout, which ffmpeg, GStreamer and faad all refused to open; CMAF put the same two bytes in its init, and the replay MP4 export in its `esds`. They now copy the source's program_config_element into that configuration. RTMP and CMAF hold the source's audio back until the first frame that carries it (about half a second on NHK's 1seg service) and publish every frame from there. If no such frame arrives within 5 s of audio, the output raises the new Warning `aac_channel_layout_missing` (categories `rtmp` and `cmaf`, output-scoped, once per wait) and goes on holding. With `audio_encode`, RTMP used to refuse such a source with only a log line and CMAF raised an `audio_encode` Warning on every frame; both now decode it. An MP4 export of a range none of whose frames carries the layout is refused with `replay_export_format_unsupported`. WebRTC Opus re-encodes now decode such a source too, and raise the same Warning, in category `webrtc`, once for the output rather than per viewer. See [transcoding.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/transcoding.md#aac-channel-layouts-the-header-does-not-name).
- **7.1 AAC targets now say 7.1.** fdk-aac's 7.1 mode is channel configuration 12, which an ADTS header cannot hold, so every `audio_encode` AAC-LC target at `channels: 8` (TS outputs, HLS, CMAF, RTMP) went out announcing 4.0 with no layout. Each 7.1 frame now announces channel configuration 0 and carries the program_config_element of its layout (centre, front pair, surround pair, rear pair, LFE), 9 bytes per frame; CMAF and RTMP carry it in the track configuration too. ffmpeg decodes it as 7.1, each input channel on its own output channel. Receivers that followed the 4.0 header now get eight channels. `audio_encode.channels: 7` (and a `transcode` block's `channels: 7` beside an AAC `audio_encode`) is now refused at config load: the AAC encoder has no 6.1 mode, and such a config used to load and then carry no audio, with a Critical `audio_encode` event. Fix any config carrying it before upgrading, or the push is refused.
- **7.1 AAC sources decode as 7.1.** The AAC decoder mixed anything wider than six channels down to 5.1, so a 7.1 AAC source re-encoded with its layout kept (no `channels` set) went out 5.1, and the display and meters saw six channels. It now hands out all eight, which the channel stage converts to what each output carries, as for E-AC-3 7.1. Needs bilbycast-fdk-aac-rs with `AacDecoder::set_max_output_channels`.
- **RTMP and WebRTC re-encode AAC sources wider than stereo.** With `audio_encode`, an RTMP output refused a 5.1 or 7.1 AAC source with only a log line and published no audio; it now re-encodes it through the channel stage, kept at its layout or converted to `channels` or the `transcode` block's, as it does an AC-3 source. A WebRTC output refused it too; it now mixes it down to stereo for its Opus stream unless a channel count is set, and does the same for an MP2, AC-3 or E-AC-3 source wider than stereo, which used to open a multichannel Opus encoder no WebRTC peer reads. Anything the WebRTC re-encode still refuses now raises a Warning `audio_encode` event.
- **A source whose AAC configuration changes mid-stream (a switch to another feed).** An RTMP output now sends a new sequence header with the first frame of the new configuration, as FLV publishers do; it used to announce the first one for the whole connection, so a receiver decoded a 44.1 kHz source switched in after a 48 kHz one as 48 kHz, 9 % fast. RTMP, CMAF and WebRTC re-encodes now rebuild their decoder for the new configuration; they used to keep the first. A CMAF passthrough output cannot follow such a change, since its init is committed, and now raises the new Warning `aac_config_changed` (category `cmaf`, output-scoped, once per change) instead of changing silently; restart it, or set `audio_encode`, where sources of different configurations are switched.
- **CMAF re-encoded AAC: raw access units, and HE-AAC tracks name their core.** Every sample of a CMAF `audio_encode` output (including `silent_fallback` silence, and the DVR renditions the manager provisions with `aac_lc` for MP2, AC-3, E-AC-3 and AAC-LATM sources) used to keep the encoder's 7-byte ADTS header inside the `mdat`. Each sample is now the raw access unit, as RTMP's are since edge#210. An `he_aac_v1` / `he_aac_v2` track's `esds` now names the core it carries (24 kHz for a 48 kHz output, mono for v2) with SBR / PS signalled implicitly, and its timescale is the core's rate, as a passed-through HE-AAC source's track always was. It used to name the output rate under AAC-LC. A `silent_fallback` track declared wider than stereo now names the stereo its encoder emits. Those tracks' inits change, as does a 7.1 track's, so such an output opens one new init generation at its first start after the upgrade, as described for HEVC above. AAC-LC targets keep their init. See [cmaf.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/cmaf.md).
- **RTMP `audio_encode` with codec `aac_lc` and no overrides now re-encodes an HE-AAC source.** That fast path passes the source's frames through untouched, and an HE-AAC source carries the AAC-LC profile in its ADTS header, so it went out as HE-AAC under a config asking for AAC-LC. The source is now told by what it decodes to and re-encoded to AAC-LC, which costs a decode and an encode for each such output. An AAC-LC source is passed through as before. See [audio-gateway.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/audio-gateway.md#same-codec-passthrough-fast-path-rtmp-only).
- **SMPTE 2022-7 SRT inputs and outputs carry on either leg, and re-acquire each leg on its own.** Each leg is accepted or dialled independently from the start, and a lost leg is re-acquired about 1 s later while the other carries on. Before this release a leg 1 down at start kept the pair off air on a healthy leg 2, and once leg 2 had blipped or missed its 15 s, a later loss of leg 1 alone took the pair off air (on an input with a false Critical `Both redundant legs lost`). The events change, so update any Routine or saved filter on the old texts. On an output, the leg-lost message becomes `SRT output '<id>' 2022-7 leg <n> lost; reconnecting` (same `error_code`, `redundancy_output_leg_lost`), and `details.other_leg` reads only `carrying` or `down`: `connecting` is gone. The `... did not connect within 15s; running single-leg` Warnings are replaced by `... 2022-7 leg <n> did not connect within 15s; still trying`, now with details `mode`, `leg`, `after_ms` and `other_leg` (`reason` / `budget_ms` are gone). On an output it covers either leg in either mode. On an input it is raised for listener legs only. A caller leg on an input latches the 5-attempt `SRT input connection failed` instead, raised by leg 2 as well as leg 1. That event is a Warning while the other leg is connected, and Critical otherwise. The input's per-leg connected Info now reads `SRT input connected (mode=<Mode>, redundant leg <n>)` for both legs, and leg 1's `details.mode` is the mode it uses, spelled `Listener` / `Caller` / `Rendezvous` like leg 2's: it used to read `listener` whatever the mode. `Redundant leg <n> lost` keeps its text and gains details `leg`, `mode` and `other_leg`. One known limit without the new `path_differential_ms` (next item): a leg that runs *ahead* of the leg carrying with a hole in it (returning on a shorter path or a lower `recv_latency_ms`, or just re-attached and skipping packets its first retransmissions missed) is not hitless. For about its lead the output interleaves two stream positions (a lead of 1024 packets or more is skipped), and neither shows in `packets_lost` or raises an event. With receive latencies set apart on purpose, every return of the lower-latency leg repeats it. Set `path_differential_ms` above the lead to merge both in order, while the lead stays under 1024 packets (about 8 Mbit/s of RTP/TS for a 1.38 s lead), or keep the legs' paths and latencies matched. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#smpte-2022-7-srt-redundancy).
- **SMPTE 2022-7 SRT inputs take `path_differential_ms`, as RTP inputs do.** Set on the input's `redundancy` block (5 to 2000 ms), it makes the pair hold every packet that long from its first arrival and release in sequence order, adding that much latency. A leg running ahead of the other with a hole (a leading leg returning, or a leg just re-attached whose first retransmissions miss their deadline) is then merged in order instead of interleaving two stream positions, which on the test rig's lossy paths showed as CC errors and PCR steps back at 9 and 11 of 139 re-attaches. Unset keeps the unbuffered merger and today's latency. Set it above the legs' receive-latency difference plus their path-delay difference. That lag must also stay under 1024 packets, the merger's window: past it a returning leading leg's lead is still skipped however long the hold, so legs at 120 ms and 1500 ms (1.38 s apart) merge in order only below about 8 Mbit/s of RTP/TS, while a re-attached leg's few-millisecond lead fits at any ordinary rate. The hold keeps at most 12 000 packets, so the rate times the hold must stay under that too (about 63 Mbit/s at the 2000 ms maximum). The merger's stats appear on the input as `buffered_hitless` while its legs carry RTP, which the manager's buffered-merger card already shows. On RTP inputs too, `buffered_hitless` is now an on-air input's own and read live, the flow's active input's, which on a PID-bus assembled flow shows only while the assembly plays from that input: a passive 2022-7 input's merger used to show under whichever input was active, and one removed or edited in place left its last values on the flow. When both legs are lost, what is held still goes out at its release time, ahead of the stream the legs bring back, or at once and in order ahead of it should the legs come back with raw TS. On raw TS it does nothing, and the `redundancy_failover_mode` Warning gains `details.path_differential_ms` to say so. SRT outputs refuse the field. Edges advertise `srt-path-differential`; an older edge accepts the field and ignores it, so a manager offering the field shows it only on edges that advertise the bit. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#smpte-2022-7-srt-redundancy).
- **SMPTE 2022-7 SRT outputs say when a leg cannot reach its peer, and drop a stale caller on a listener leg.** A caller leg now raises `srt_output_peer_unreachable`, as a single-leg caller output does: `SRT output '<id>' 2022-7 leg <n> cannot reach its peer — <n> consecutive connection attempts failed, still retrying`, at the fifth failed attempt and every twentieth after, counted afresh on every acquisition of the leg. It is a Warning while the other leg is attached and Critical otherwise, with `leg`, `mode` and `other_leg` in its details, and leg 1's attempts now drive the output's `connect_failed` state. Before, a caller leg said only that its first acquisition had not connected within 15 s, and a lost leg whose peer never came back said nothing more. A listener leg now judges each caller by the ACKs to its own first sends: with none within 3 s it raises the new Warning `SRT output '<id>' 2022-7 leg <n> stale connection detected`, drops the caller and accepts the next at once, with no leg-lost Warning and no `disconnected`. A connection the listener queued while the leg was attached, whose caller libsrt has since given up, is closed on accept with no event. Before, a leg sent into a stale caller until the peer idle timeout (30 s by default), and attached and lost a given-up one at its first send. The single-leg `cannot reach its peer` message also loses a run of 26 spaces after its dash, so update a Routine or saved filter that matches the old text exactly.
- **SMPTE 2022-7 SRT inputs with `path_differential_ms` check the legs' SSRCs, as RTP inputs do, and neither counts a source changing its SSRC any more.** `buffered_hitless.ssrc_mismatch` counts legs that go on carrying RTP under different SSRCs, and each rise raises the Warning `redundancy_ssrc_mismatch`; on an SRT input it used to read 0 whatever the legs carried. On both input types a mismatch now counts only once the legs have disagreed for the merger's stale time (a second past `path_differential_ms`, plus on an SRT pair the legs' receive-latency difference) with both delivering, once per episode. A source that changes its SSRC changes it on both legs, whose copies of the change arrive apart, and an RTP input used to count one and raise the Warning at every such change, an upstream Take between RTP sources included. Losing both legs of an SRT pair forgets the SSRCs, so a sender restarting on a new one counts none.
- **SMPTE 2022-7 SRT inputs drop a stale caller on a listener leg.** A listener leg that has delivered nothing 3 s plus its TSBPD delay after the other leg first delivered since its accept, with the other leg still delivering, raises the new Warning `SRT input 2022-7 leg <n> stale connection detected` and is dropped and re-accepted at once, with no `Redundant leg <n> lost`. Nothing is judged while the other leg is down or silent, so a healthy leg of a silent source is never dropped. A connection the listener queued while the leg was attached, whose caller has since given it up, is closed on accept with no event. Before, a stale accept held the leg until the peer idle timeout (30 s by default) while the caller's new connection waited behind it, and a given-up one was attached, announced and lost at once.
- **Single-channel DeckLink SDI hosts: refresh the systemd unit.** The packaged unit now grants `/dev/blackmagic/dv0`…`dv7` beside `io0`…`io7`. Before, a host whose cards expose `dvN` nodes (single-channel DeckLink SDI) enumerated no cards under the unit and offered no SDI. A manager-driven upgrade replaces only the binary, so add the grants in a drop-in (`sudo systemctl edit bilbycast-edge`, one `DeviceAllow=/dev/blackmagic/dvN rw` line per node, then `sudo systemctl restart bilbycast-edge`), or refresh the unit with `install-edge.sh --upgrade-installer` (which also moves the node to the latest release) and restart. The boot log's `sdi.decklink` warning now names any device node the edge cannot open. See [docs/sdi.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/sdi.md#checklist-c--grant-the-device-nodes-under-systemd), Checklist C.
- **Continuity counters once more show loss after an input switch or a source PCR step.** On a passthrough flow, the continuity fixer used to renumber every CC after the first Take, or after the first source PCR step over 500 ms (which an outage that long causes on default settings), for the rest of the flow, so no later loss showed. CCs now pass through as the source sent them, except on PAT and PMT under the default muxer-mode clock, whose rewriter numbers those two PIDs itself, so loss on them still does not show. A flow that has been losing packets since a Take or an outage, including drops inside the edge, will count them in the flow's TR 101 290 `cc_errors` and in content-analysis MDI MLR, and may raise the `tr101290_p1` health reason ("continuity-counter errors", Error); that loss was always there. Legal duplicate packets go out as duplicates. A source that restarts its counters at each loop, and replay seeks, show one CC error per PID at each event, as they already did before the first. The cut itself is unchanged: one CC jump per PID, PAT/PMT injection and DI. See [architecture.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/architecture.md).
- **SRT inputs with `passthrough_clock: true` keep their sender-timestamp rate source after such a step.** After the first Take or source PCR step over 500 ms, nearly every datagram the fixer forwarded (every one holding a non-null packet) lost its SRT sender timestamp, so the flow's PLL lost its sender-timestamp reference for the rest of the flow: it took its rate from PCR instead, or, on a CBR-padded source whose all-null datagrams kept theirs, switched between the two and re-anchored. Forwarded datagrams now keep every field they arrived with, including the one that carries the discontinuity indicator. This applies only to a flow whose master clock is the PLL (auto on a single-input SRT flow, or an explicit `contribution` / `source_pcr_pll` / `sender_timestamp` kind on a switcher) and whose SRT input has `passthrough_clock: true` and no `program_number`, `pid_overrides`, `pid_map` or ingress transcode: on default settings the muxer-mode clock rewriter already drops the sender timestamp at ingress, so the PLL runs on PCR before and after the upgrade. The flow's `master_clock.rate_source` now says which one fed it (next item). See [clocking.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/clocking.md).
- **New flow stats field `master_clock.rate_source`.** While a flow's master clock is the source-PCR PLL, it names what fed the PLL its last rate sample: `sender_timestamp` (the SRT sender's per-packet timestamp), `pcr` (a PCR read from the bytes) or `none` (no sample yet). It is absent on every other clock kind and on a fallback rung. A flow configured for `sender_timestamp` that reads `pcr` is running on PCR: on default settings the muxer-mode clock rewriter drops the sender timestamp at ingress, so only an SRT input with `passthrough_clock: true` and no other ingress stage delivers it, and RIST carries none. The edge computed this before but dropped it on the way into the stats. A manager can show it beside the clock kind. See [metrics.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/metrics.md#master-clock-telemetry-flowstatsmaster_clock).
- **A flow whose master clock is `sender_timestamp` or `contribution` now says so on `master_clock.configured_kind`.** Both run the source-PCR PLL and report `kind` `source_pcr_pll`; the configured kind they were meant to carry beside it was never filled in, so a sender-timestamp flow read exactly like a plain `source_pcr_pll` pin. An explicit `source_pcr_pll` still carries no `configured_kind`.
- **SRT outputs that transcode start each new connection on the live programme.** A listener, caller or bonded SRT output with `audio_encode` or `video_encode` kept its transcode chain from one connection to the next. A re-joining caller first got TS the last one never did, then a PCR jump the length of the reconnection gap (a second or more) with no discontinuity indicator, with the audio held from before the gap stamped for after it. A receiving edge bridged that jump and stepped its audio PTS by about a second (`source_pts_discontinuity` on the audio PID 1.4 to 1.6 s after the join, on 3 of 6 re-joins on the test rig). Now each connection drops what the chain still holds from the last one and resets the re-encoders as an input switch does, reopening the video encoder too, so no picture it still held from the last connection reaches the new one: the new receiver's first PCR is the live programme's, its audio starts on the same timeline, and its video starts on an IDR at its own timestamps. `cbr_pad_to_kbps` starts afresh too, where it sent the gap's worth of NULL packets in bursts with the new connection's first chunks. A transcoding SRT output also now passes on everything its chain has ready each time round, not one chunk per chunk given to it, so chunks the chain produces late (a bursty source, a slow encode) no longer stay queued, adding to the output's latency for as long as it runs. Nothing changes for an output that does not transcode or pad. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#srt-output).
- **RIST outputs that transcode hand on everything their transcode chain has ready.** A RIST output with `audio_encode` or `video_encode` took one chunk from its chain per chunk it gave it, as SRT outputs did, so chunks the chain produced while the output ran ahead of it (a bursty source, a slow encode) stayed queued for as long as the output ran, adding to its latency. It now takes everything ready each time round, as UDP and RTP outputs do. A transcoding RIST output's latency may drop after the upgrade. See [transcoding.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/transcoding.md).
- **Outputs that demux the TS let go of an audio, video or SCTE-35 stream a PMT update drops.** When the program's PMT stopped listing any audio stream, its video or its SCTE-35 PID, the shared demuxer (RTMP, CMAF, WebRTC, the local display, SDI and the other re-muxing outputs) stayed on the old PID: the output went on reporting and expecting that track (the display overlay named the old video PID), and demuxed whatever still came on the PID as its audio, video or cues. It now selects none until a PMT lists the stream again, which is then picked up afresh. See [transcoding.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/transcoding.md#source_audio_pid--pinning-the-source-track).
- **`fec_decode` inputs started mid-stream no longer publish made-up packets.** An RTP input with `fec_decode` (single-leg or a 2022-7 leg) that starts while its sender is already running — a node or flow restart, an upgrade, `add_input` — applied FEC received before its first media packet to the first matrix it opened, publishing rebuilt packets with bytes never sent, or a real packet a second time, and counting them in `packets_recovered_fec`. Such FEC is now discarded. Works with old and new senders. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#smpte-2022-1-fec-configuration).
- **`fec_decode` inputs keep repairing across a reordered or late packet.** An RTP input with `fec_decode` (single-leg or a 2022-7 leg) took any datagram behind its open FEC matrix for the start of a new one, discarding the open matrix's datagrams and the FEC still to come for them. A reorder across a matrix boundary, or the late original of a datagram FEC had already rebuilt, therefore cost the next matrix its repairs: at 4 x 4, a datagram delayed by four places left a loss in the next matrix's last row unpublished. A datagram less than a matrix behind is now taken as late: it is published as before, the open matrix keeps everything it holds, and a matrix's own first datagram arriving after its second is taken into it. A single-leg input no longer passes a duplicate to the decoder at all. A step back of a whole matrix or more still starts a new matrix. Nothing changes on the wire. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#smpte-2022-1-fec-configuration).
- **`fec_decode` inputs close two more ways to rebuild a packet from bytes never sent.** A matrix that every datagram has reached is now closed to anything more until the next one opens: a sender restarting a few numbers back into it used to have its second copy filed there, and with two columns the row FEC sent after the original rebuilt a packet that was never sent, with no loss at all. FEC naming another base inside the window drops the FEC held for the old base rather than applying it to the realigned matrix. A duplicated header-only datagram no longer counts twice towards completing a matrix, which closed it with a datagram still missing, losing that datagram's repair. A rebuilt datagram's RTP header now comes from the newest datagram filed in the matrix, not from a late one left out of it. Nothing changes on the wire. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#smpte-2022-1-fec-configuration).
- **`fec_encode` outputs no longer drop a matrix's protection for one late packet.** An RTP output forwarding RTP (a 2022-7 output fed by an RTP input) that met a sequence number behind its open FEC matrix started a new matrix there, leaving the open one's columns and rows without FEC. Such a datagram now goes out unprotected and the open matrix is protected in full. Works with old and new receivers.
- **Muxer-mode PCR padding now keeps every PCR interval within 40 ms.** When the gap to the next source PCR exceeds 40 ms (a sparse-PCR source, or PCR-bearing datagrams lost upstream), the clock rewriter fills it with synthetic PCRs. It injected one fewer than needed whenever the gap was not a whole multiple of 40 ms, so a 45 ms gap (two lost datagrams of a 15 ms-PCR source) got none and a 90 ms gap kept a 50 ms interval, failing TR 101 290 PCR_RR. It now injects as many as the gap needs, evenly spaced. The synthetic PCRs still go out with the next source PCR, immediately ahead of it.
- **RTMP, CMAF, WebRTC and HLS outputs honour `audio_encode.source_audio_pid`, and RTMP, CMAF and WebRTC say when they cannot publish their audio.** Up to 0.116.0 these outputs ignored the pin: RTMP, CMAF and WebRTC published the program's first audio stream of any codec, and HLS the last one it could decode. An output that carries a pin now publishes the pinned track, so check before upgrading that each pin names the track you want. Unpinned, RTMP, CMAF and WebRTC now publish the program's first audio stream they can publish (without `audio_encode`, the first they pass through, AAC or on WebRTC Opus, ahead of one they would have to re-encode, so an ATSC program carrying AC-3 then AAC publishes its AAC where it published nothing), and its first of any codec only when there is none, so an MPTS whose first audio track is AC-4 (or Opus-in-TS, on RTMP and CMAF) is published from the track behind it (re-encoded through `audio_encode` when that is MP2, AC-3, E-AC-3 or AAC-LATM, or AAC on WebRTC), where it used to publish silence. None of the three can publish AC-4, RTMP and CMAF cannot publish Opus-in-TS, and on a build without `media-codecs` RTMP and CMAF publish only AAC and WebRTC only Opus and AAC. A pin is taken only onto a track the output can publish. One the PMT does not carry, or in a codec the output cannot publish, leaves the output on the track it would take unpinned (on HLS, the last one it can decode) and raises the Warning `audio_source_pid_not_found` whenever that is not the pin, once per output and fallback track (a WebRTC output raises it once, not per viewer). An RTMP, CMAF or WebRTC output left on a track it cannot publish, because the program carries none it can, still publishes none of the source's audio, but now raises the Warning `audio_codec_unpublishable` naming the PID and codec, once per episode, in its own category (`rtmp`, `cmaf`, `webrtc`); a WebRTC output raises it once, not per viewer, and not when `video_only`. Under `silent_fallback` RTMP and WebRTC now lay silence on such a track, which an AC-4 track used to hold off. See [transcoding.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/transcoding.md#source_audio_pid--pinning-the-source-track).
- **An SRT input no longer takes a flow's idle keepalive for its payload format.** While its active input is silent (at flow start until the source delivers, and through any gap, such as a file loop) a flow publishes a keepalive of NULL packets, which is raw TS whatever the input's framing, and an SRT output sent it in among RTP. An SRT input settles RTP/TS or raw TS once, on its first datagram. When that was a keepalive from an RTP-framed sender, it settled raw TS and published every RTP datagram with its RTP header inside the TS: corrupt output until the input restarted (on a 2022-7 pair, until both legs dropped), with a false Warning `redundancy_failover_mode`. An SRT input now settles on the first datagram that is not NULL packets alone, and drops such datagrams uncounted until then, whoever sends them. A 2022-7 SRT input fed data that is neither RTP nor TS now takes it for raw TS once, as a single-socket input does, and raises `redundancy_failover_mode` once rather than on every datagram. An SRT output now sends the keepalive only once its media has gone out raw TS: never into an RTP-framed stream, and not before its first media datagram, so a receiver that connects to a silent flow gets nothing until the source delivers (SRT keeps the connection up with its own keepalive). With nothing to send, an SRT output still notices a lost peer, a lost 2022-7 leg or a failed bonded group, and redials. A listener-mode SRT output's 3 s liveness probe now runs from the first datagram it sends, not from the accept. One whose input is silent when a caller connects has nothing to send it, so it keeps the connection; a stale one is now dropped on the peer idle timeout (`peer_idle_timeout_secs`, 30 s by default) instead of within 3 s. One that transcodes, runs SMPTE 302M, filters a program, rewrites PIDs or delays its stream runs no probe and judges the caller by the ACKs to its own first datagrams instead, with the same 3 s: its probe sent a new caller up to 3 s of the flow as published ahead of its own stream, such as an RTP input's datagrams ahead of a transcoding output's raw TS, which a receiver that settles its framing on the first datagram then dropped. Media analysis no longer reports `payload_format` `raw_ts` for an RTP flow whose keepalive it saw first. An upgraded input is safe with any sender, and an upgraded output protects older receivers. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#srt-input).
- **A multi-input flow carries one framing whichever input is on air, and a Take's PSI goes out in the framing of the input switched to.** On a Take to an RTP-framed input, the PAT and PMT the continuity fixer injects now go out as RTP datagrams in that input's own stream (its SSRC, numbered just ahead of its first datagram). They went out as raw TS whatever the input's framing, so on an RTP-framed flow an SRT receiver that connected or reconnected around a Take could settle raw TS on them and drop every RTP datagram after. A flow switching between an RTP-framed input and a raw-TS one (an RTP contribution with a media-player slate, say) now keeps the framing of its first media datagram until it restarts: an RTP input on a raw-TS flow loses its RTP header, and a raw-TS input on an RTP-framed flow goes out under an RTP header of the flow's own (its own SSRC and sequence numbers, six TS packets to a datagram). Before, each input went out in its own framing, and an SRT output carried both on one connection. A flow whose inputs share one framing is unchanged. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#multi-input-flows-and-seamless-switching).
- **SMPTE 2022-7 RTP outputs send every datagram under one SSRC and sequence of their own.** An RTP-framed flow's datagrams went out with their upstream RTP header, while the raw-TS keepalives the output sent through an input gap went out under its own SSRC and numbers, so a receiver saw two streams interleaved. The 2022-7 path now re-wraps RTP as the single-leg path always has, so its numbers are contiguous and its FEC follows them; an upstream's gaps in numbering no longer show in the output's sequence numbers (continuity counters in the TS still show them). A receiver keyed on the upstream SSRC or sequence numbers sees the output's instead: in particular a downstream 2022-7 input, or seq-aware Hitless slot, merging this output with another edge's relay of the same source no longer merges. That could only ever work on a flow passing the source's bytes unchanged (`passthrough_clock: true`, no program filter or PID rewrite) and never across the keepalives, and no documented setup relies on it; the two legs of one 2022-7 output still carry identical datagrams. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#smpte-2022-1-fec-configuration).
- **SRT outputs carry RTP datagrams larger than one live message whole.** An SRT output sends each item as one live message of at most 1316 bytes and cut anything longer into 1316-byte chunks, so a seven-packet RTP datagram from an RTP/UDP SMPTE 2022-2 input (1328 bytes) left as 1316 bytes and a 12-byte tail with no RTP header, and RTP over SRT from such a source was unreadable. Now, from the first RTP datagram that does not fit, the output numbers the stream itself: every RTP datagram after it goes out as datagrams of up to six TS packets under the output's own SSRC and contiguous sequence numbers, with the source's timestamp. The stream's SSRC changes once when that happens; an RTP-over-SRT source of six-packet datagrams, which fits, is still relayed with its own numbers. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#srt-output).
- **An SRT input follows a sender that changes payload format.** A single-socket SRT input (listener, caller or bonded) kept the format it settled on first for its whole life, across reconnects, so a sender restarted with the other framing, or an input that settled on a misleading first datagram, was dropped for good. It now re-settles after 50 datagrams in a row clearly in the other framing, raising the new Warning `srt_payload_format_changed` (details `from` and `to`, `rtp_ts` or `raw_ts`), and drops such datagrams until then. A few stray datagrams of the other framing, such as the raw PSI an older bilbycast sender puts into an RTP stream at a Take, never move it. A 2022-7 pair still settles afresh only after both legs are lost. See [events-and-alarms.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/events-and-alarms.md#srt-srt).
- **One DI per new time base, every program's on an MPTS Take, and none on audio or ancillary flows.** The source-discontinuity watch no longer arms a second DI, one PCR later, for a jumped PCR that already carries one: in muxer mode the clock rewriter stamps a DI on every jump it sees, and the fixer stamps one on a Take, so every source jump on a default flow, and every Take between `passthrough_clock` or bonded inputs on different epochs, used to put two DIs on the output for one new time base. `source_pcr_discontinuity` is still raised and counted. On a Take to an MPTS the fixer now marks the first PCR of every program, where only the first PCR of any one program took it and the watch stamped the others a PCR late. A Take the fixer's queue is too full to take goes with the input's next packet rather than being lost. Inputs that carry no MPEG-TS (ST 2110-30, -31 and -40, `rtp_audio`, MXL audio without `audio_encode`) now pass the continuity fixer byte for byte, send no TS NULL keepalive while silent (their outputs used to be handed one every 250 ms), and a flow made only of them runs no watcher: before, a PCM or ANC byte pattern that happened to read as a PCR could take a DI bit or raise `source_pcr_discontinuity`. See [clocking.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/clocking.md#source-discontinuities-on-an-mpts).
- **WHEP inputs carry the server's Opus audio, and WebRTC inputs lay their TS out from what the peer sends.** A WHEP input used to mux the video track alone: an A/V pull lost its audio, and a pull of a server sending no video (another edge's WHEP output on an audio-only flow, which accepts H.264 all the same) published nothing but NULL keepalives, its flow reporting the input stalled. Both WebRTC inputs now lay the TS out from the tracks the session negotiated, then from what the peer sends: a track that has sent nothing by the time the other has run 1 s leaves the PMT with a version bump, the PCR moving to the audio when the video leaves, and comes back with its first frame. So a WHEP pull or a WHIP publish of audio alone carries no PCR for its first second (a WHIP publisher that offered a camera and sent none used to carry no PCR at all), and one of video alone lists an Opus stream for its first second. A track a WHIP publish negotiates after its media began now joins the PMT with a version bump, audio included. The pull's timestamps now start 100 ms in, both tracks on one timeline, instead of at the server's raw RTP timestamp. Outputs of a WHEP-input flow now receive Opus where the server sends it: RTMP and CMAF outputs, which cannot publish Opus-in-TS, raise `audio_codec_unpublishable` for it, and a WebRTC output passes it through. An answer that accepts neither H.264 nor Opus, or that the input cannot apply, now raises a Warning `whep_answer_unusable` once per episode and is pulled again after the backoff; the latter was a log line only. Each pull's resource on the server is now released with a DELETE when the pull ends, in the background and bounded to 10 s; before, every reconnect left one to the server's own timeout. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md#whep-input).
- **An `audio_encode` re-encodes Opus-in-TS.** The TS audio replacer took Opus for a codec it cannot decode and passed it through, raising `audio_transcode_source_not_found` with reason `codec_not_replaceable`, so an ingress `audio_encode` on a WHIP or WHEP input, whose audio is always Opus, re-encoded nothing. It now decodes a single mono or stereo Opus stream (the "Opus" registration descriptor, with no Opus extension descriptor or one naming channel configuration 1 or 2) and re-encodes it to the configured codec, on inputs and on SRT / UDP / RTP / RIST outputs alike, so a flow carrying Opus with an `audio_encode` now goes out in the configured codec, with the PMT naming it and the Opus descriptors dropped. Multistream Opus (more than two channels, or dual mono) still passes through with that reason. See [transcoding.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/transcoding.md#source_audio_pid--pinning-the-source-track).
- **Buffered SMPTE 2022-7 stats: late copies are split from late loss, and the measured skew can read above the hold.** On an RTP or SRT 2022-7 input with `path_differential_ms`, `buffered_hitless.late_dropped` used to count every copy that arrived after the hold had released past it, most of them harmless copies of packets the other leg had already delivered. It now counts only real loss, a gap fill that came too late or a copy too far back to tell, and the harmless ones count in the new `late_duplicates`. `max_observed_path_diff_us` and `current_path_diff_us` measured only copies that met within the hold, so they never read above `max_path_diff_ms` however far apart the legs were (a bench read 77 ms behind a 100 ms hold with about 300 ms of real skew). They now measure late copies too, so after the upgrade a reading above the hold is the skew to raise `path_differential_ms` past. Dashboards or alarms on `late_dropped` will see it fall on such inputs. The hold also no longer allocates on the media path. See [api-reference.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/api-reference.md).
- **SMPTE 2022-7 SRT inputs label low-rate loss correctly and count loss in flight when both legs go.** Below about 34 packets a second, every packet both legs' SRT dropped too late was reported as upstream loss (`packet_loss`) rather than `srt_recv_dropped`, and a burst long enough to re-anchor the merger could be undercounted; that now holds only below about 5 packets a second. When both legs are lost, the gaps the merger was still waiting for the later leg to fill now count as lost, and loss still waiting for the legs' stats polls is counted at once. Before, a source that never came back left it uncounted. `packets_lost` can therefore read slightly higher than before after an outage of both legs.
- **Creating an input checks it against seq-aware Hitless slots that already name it, and `add_input` saves the definition that runs.** A flow can be created naming a Hitless leg that is not defined yet. `POST /api/v1/inputs` and the WS `create_input` now refuse an input created under such a name that would reach the PID bus without the sequence number the slot merges on (`hitless_seq_aware_leg_unsequenced`), as an update already did; before, it was created and only the merger's fallback to primary preference caught it. A WS `add_input` of an input the node already has now saves the definition it was sent, keeping the input's `active` flag; before, the flow ran the definition sent while `config.json` kept the old one. A WS `add_input` of an input another enabled flow already holds is now refused (`validation_error`, "already assigned to another flow") before anything starts or is saved; before, it was saved in both flows and the next load refused the config. The same goes for an enabled flow taking such an input through `POST /api/v1/flows`, `PUT /api/v1/flows/ID` (HTTP 400) or the WS `create_flow`, `update_flow`, `start_flow` and `restart_flow`. `POST /api/v1/flows/ID/restart` and IS-05 receiver activation now read the configuration only once the old run has stopped, so a plan swap saved during the restart is no longer saved beside a flow running another plan. An IS-05 activation whose flow no longer resolves after the change now reports the failure (Critical event, HTTP 500) as a failed restart already did, instead of leaving the flow stopped with an "activated" event.
- **Seq-aware Hitless mergers follow the holds their legs actually run with, and SMPTE 2022-7 SRT inputs the latency each leg negotiated.** A PID-bus seq-aware slot's merger sizes its stale time to how far its legs lag; it read the legs' holds from the configuration only when the slot's flow started or swapped its plan, so an edit to a leg's input on a host flow reached it only then, and a plan swap after a `tuning.ingress_dejitter_ms` push, which running RTP inputs do not take until they restart, read a hold no input had and restarted the slot's merger on air. The merger now follows each leg's input as it starts, and a swap that leaves the slot alone keeps it. A 2022-7 SRT input now reads each leg's latency as libsrt negotiated it once the leg connects, so a sender asking for more latency than the edge no longer lets the later leg be taken for a moved stream, and while one leg's socket is down a moved stream is followed after a second rather than after the legs' latency difference as well. On the PID bus, a moved stream with one leg up still waits out the legs' lag plus a second, which is inherent. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md).
- **Re-encoded audio keeps the audio before a seam on its own timeline.** At a source PTS jump (a `media_player` loop, an input switch, a gap) an output that re-encodes audio used to stamp the last 2048 samples before the jump, the AAC-LC encoder's delay, after it: 42.7 ms per seam presented late by the whole jump (+320 ms at each loop of a file whose audio ends 320 ms before its picture). On RTMP, CMAF, HLS and WebRTC the encoder now runs that audio out under the old timestamps first, then starts the new timeline one frame before its first PTS. Each seam therefore ends the old audio with up to one frame of silence on its own timeline, and the part frame of audio the encoder held at the seam (up to 21 ms) is no longer dropped. On TS outputs fed by a `media_player` input the timestamp step now lands on the first frame whose audio is past it, and at a source step of more than 500 ms the audio before it stays on the old timeline. A CMAF encoder rebuilt for another source rate no longer drops the end of the audio before the change. See [transcoding.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/transcoding.md).
- **A `media_player` file cut mid-PES no longer glues its first audio packets onto the previous file's last frame.** A capture's leading continuation packets (the tail of a PES whose start is not in the file) now go nowhere on every elementary stream, as they already did on the video. At a loop or playlist splice they were appended to the previous file's truncated last frame, so every output re-encoding that track decoded a burst of up to full scale once per loop (14 ms on a capture whose last E-AC-3 frame is 349 of its 512 bytes). The edge's own decoders now drop the truncated frame. A passthrough output still forwards that truncated last PES as the file has it. See [configuration-guide.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/configuration-guide.md).
- **The first packet on each PID after a flow start or restart carries the discontinuity indicator.** Under the default muxer-mode clock, a restarted flow's first packet on a PID could carry the previous instance's last continuity counter with other bytes (about 1 restart in 16 per PID), which a strict receiver drops as a duplicate: the first audio PES after 7 of 20 restarts on a bench. The first packet the flow's rewriter sends on each PID now sets `discontinuity_indicator`, in its adaptation field or on an adaptation-field-only packet just ahead of it, so one extra 188-byte packet per PID can appear at a start. Inputs with `passthrough_clock: true` are unchanged. See [clocking.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/clocking.md).
- **WebRTC re-encoded audio follows the source's timeline, as RTMP and CMAF do.** A WHEP viewer or WHIP output with `audio_encode` used to anchor its Opus encoder on its first frame and count samples from there, so a loop whose audio ends before its picture put the audio's RTP time further behind the picture's at every lap (1.3 s after three laps of a 2 s loop with a 320 ms audio hole), and an input switch kept the old feed's A/V relation. The encoder is now re-anchored where the source leaves it, and `silent_fallback` silence is laid to the newest picture instead of running from RTP time 0, so a video-only source's silence carries the picture's time. No silence is sent before the session has seen a picture or audio. See [transcoding.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/transcoding.md).
- **TR 101 290 `cc_errors` no longer counts a continuity break the stream signals with `discontinuity_indicator`.** ISO/IEC 13818-1 lets the CC break on such a packet, or after an adaptation-field-only packet carrying the indicator, and TR 101 290's CC_error does not count it. The flow's `cc_errors` (and `window_cc_errors`, `bilbycast_edge_tr101290_cc_errors_total`) used to. A Take whose first packet on a PID carries the switch's DI, and an input restart within a running flow, now count one fewer per such PID. Unsignalled breaks are counted as before. See [metrics.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/metrics.md).

## Upgrading from v0.115.0 or earlier

<!-- Static text: remove once no supported upgrade starts at v0.115.0 or earlier. -->
- **`PUT /api/v1/config` keeps the secrets its body leaves out.** `GET /api/v1/config` leaves out every infrastructure secret. Putting that body back used to empty the node secret, `server.auth`, `server.tls` and the tunnel keys, and the next save stranded the node at its restart. Now:
  - a secret the body leaves out is kept, and one it names `null` is removed;
  - a body that names `setup_token` is refused with 400;
  - a tunnel the body adds or changes is refused with 400 without the key its mode needs (relay: `tunnel_encryption_key`, direct: `tunnel_psk`);
  - a body that does not parse is 400, where it was 422.

  A script that removed a secret by leaving it out must now send `null`. See [api-reference.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/api-reference.md#put-apiv1config).
- **A registration survives a restart.** The node keeps the node ID it registered under in `secrets.json` beside its secret, so a registration whose `config.json` write failed still authenticates after a restart, and the setup wizard stays closed. A credential save that fails raises the new Warning event `manager_credentials_not_saved`.
- **Pair with bilbycast-manager v0.90.0 for whole downloads at the retention limit.** With that manager, a Replay recording at its retention limit downloads whole: each chunk is read from where the last one ended, so retention removing segments already delivered no longer fails the download. With an older manager, a recording retention has already pruned is refused at the first chunk, as before. Every pairing works.
- **Recorder and CMAF intake queues are bounded in bytes, per queue and node-wide.** Each recorder and each CMAF output queues at most 32 MiB, within 256 MiB for all recorders and 256 MiB for all CMAF outputs on the node. A node whose replay disk or origin cannot keep up drops past those limits and counts the drops in `packets_dropped`.
- **A recording one config push moves between flows is handed over.** When two flows name one `storage_id`, the flow taking the recording waits for the other to let it go. If the other flow is still running 30 s later, it is refused with `replay_recording_in_use`.

## Upgrading from v0.114.1 or earlier

<!-- Static text: remove once no supported upgrade starts at v0.114.1 or earlier. -->
- **Upgrade the manager to v0.89.0 first** (or together). This edge can answer a flow-assembly swap with `pid_bus_assembly_unconfirmed` (the plan was saved and goes on air once the assembler resumes); the v0.88.1 AI assistant reads that as "nothing changed" and reports the plan rolled back. v0.89.0 reverses and audits it.
- **Seq-aware Hitless slots are now checked.** A `seq_aware` slot with a leg that carries no sequence number (any leg but RTP or RIST, or an RTP/RIST leg behind an ingress transcode, `program_number`, `pid_overrides` or `pid_map`, or on a flow with no assembly without `passthrough_clock: true`) is switched to `primary_preference` at the first start, `config.json` is rewritten, and a Warning `config` event names it (`hitless_seq_aware_leg_unsequenced`). A whole-config push of the manager's cached copy is repaired the same way; a targeted edit that carries such a slot (a flow or input edit, an assembly swap, `add_input`) is refused with that code, so fix the slot in the manager before editing those flows.
- **A seq-aware slot's `reorder_window` now takes effect.** The merger used to run 1024 whatever was configured, so a slot set lower now accepts fewer late gap fills. Review it before upgrading.
- **SRT loss is now counted.** libsrt's too-late drops reach `packets_lost` and a new `srt_recv_dropped` health reason (Warning, Error past 100) while the input is on air, and SMPTE 2022-7 SRT inputs report both legs and the pair's loss for the first time. Flows that were losing packets silently can raise alarms after the upgrade.

## Upgrading from v0.114.0 or earlier

<!-- Static text: remove once no supported upgrade starts at v0.114.0 or earlier. -->
The manager's **Upgrade** button cannot move an edge on v0.114.0 or earlier onto this release. Those edges' upgrade check refuses every genuine release: v0.105.0 to v0.114.0 with `upgrade_identity_not_allowed` (it compared the wrong certificate field with its allowlist), older edges with `upgrade_signature_invalid`. It failed closed, so nothing unverified was ever installed, but the fix is in this binary, so move each such edge onto it **once** by hand:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/releases/latest/download/install-edge.sh \
  | sudo bash -s -- --upgrade-installer
sudo systemctl restart bilbycast-edge
```

A plain re-run of `install-edge.sh` on an installed node changes nothing; `--upgrade-installer` installs the latest release and points `current` at it, leaving `config.json` and `secrets.json` alone. From then on the Upgrade button works. See [docs/upgrade.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/upgrade.md).

## Upgrading from v0.113.0 or earlier

<!-- Static text: remove once no supported upgrade starts at v0.113.0 or earlier. -->
Upgrade every edge that carries a **WebRTC WHIP output** first, then the relays and the edges with **WHIP inputs** it publishes into. A WHIP output on v0.113.0 or earlier panics on the answer a current relay or edge gives it and stops publishing until its flow restarts; a current WHIP output publishing into an older relay or edge works. See [supported-protocols.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/supported-protocols.md#webrtc-whipwhep).

## Binaries

Asset filenames carry no version, so `https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/releases/latest/download/<asset>` always resolves to the latest release. Each tarball unpacks to a versioned directory, `bilbycast-edge-{{VERSION}}-<artefact>/`, where `<artefact>` is `x86_64-linux-full`, `aarch64-linux-full` or `aarch64-linux-rockchip`.

Each artefact carries the video encoders and hardware decoders its platform can use; the hardware decoders serve both the transcode input path and the local-display output. At start-up the edge probes which of them the host can actually open: NVENC and NVDEC with an NVIDIA driver, QSV (encode and decode) on an Intel iGPU with its media runtime, VAAPI where a VAAPI driver is installed (Mesa radeonsi for AMD, iHD for Intel), and RKMPP on Rockchip. x264 / x265 and libavcodec software decode cover everything else. Every artefact is an **AGPL-3.0-or-later combined work** that bundles GPL-2.0-or-later code — see `NOTICE` inside the tarball.

- `bilbycast-edge-x86_64-linux-full.tar.gz` — Linux x86_64 (amd64). Encoders: x264, x265, NVENC, QSV, VAAPI. Hardware decode: NVDEC, QSV, VAAPI.
- `bilbycast-edge-aarch64-linux-full.tar.gz` — Linux ARM64 (aarch64). Encoders: x264, x265, NVENC, VAAPI. Hardware decode: NVDEC, VAAPI. No QSV: Intel iGPUs are x86_64-only.
- `bilbycast-edge-aarch64-linux-rockchip.tar.gz` — Linux ARM64 for **Rockchip RK3568 / RK3588** boards (NanoPi R5S/R6S, Orange Pi 5, Radxa Rock 5B…). Encoders: **RKMPP** H.264 / HEVC (`h264_rkmpp` / `hevc_rkmpp`, 8-bit 4:2:0 only), with x264 / x265 as the CPU fallback for 10-bit and 4:2:2. Hardware decode: RKMPP, plus the **RGA** hardware frame copy on the local-display path. No NVENC, QSV or VAAPI. **`install-edge.sh` cannot install this artefact**: on a Rockchip board it installs `aarch64-linux-full`, which has no RKMPP and no RGA, so install this one by hand ([installation guide](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/installation.md), "ARM Rockchip SBCs"). Once a node runs it, remote upgrade keeps selecting it (upgrade variant `rockchip`).

**MXL** (Media eXchange Layer) support is compiled in. MXL is a shared-memory IPC protocol — the edge discovers the system-installed `libmxl.so` at runtime via `dlopen` and advertises MXL capabilities only when the library is present. Install MXL system-wide so all MXL-speaking applications on the host share the same library.

**Multiviewer** (mosaic compositor + stream head) is compiled into all three artefacts. A wall composites node-local inputs onto one canvas — up to 1920x1080 in this phase — and publishes it as an ordinary MPEG-TS flow source, so it restreams over SRT / RTP / UDP / WebRTC / CMAF, records, nests inside another wall and produces thumbnails with no extra output configuration. Unlike SDI and MXL there is nothing to install: every artefact already carries the encoder the canvas needs, so nodes running these binaries advertise the `mv-compositor` capability and the manager's wall surfaces appear automatically. Confirm with `bilbycast-edge --print-capabilities`. The canvas is encoded by whichever backend the **host** can actually open: the wall's `codec` (default `h264_auto`) resolves against the probed hardware, hardware first and CPU last, so QuickSync leads on an Intel host, NVENC on NVIDIA, VAAPI on AMD, RKMPP on RK3568/RK3588, and libx264 where there is no hardware encoder. Measured on an Intel Core Ultra 9 285HX: `h264_auto` → `["h264_qsv", "h264_vaapi", "x264"]`. Before v0.106.0 every wall was encoded on CPU libx264 whatever the host had, and the requested codec was ignored (edge #129).

{{SDI_NOTE}}

### Runtime requirements

The binaries need **glibc 2.39 or newer**: Ubuntu 24.04 or later, Debian 13 or later. They will not start on Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12.

libx264 and libx265 are **statically linked**, so no `libx264` / `libx265` package is needed and the binary is not tied to a distro's ABI-versioned `libx264.so.<build>` / `libx265.so.<build>`. The binary does link these system libraries, and will not start without them:

| Artefact | Libraries | Packages (Ubuntu / Debian) |
|---|---|---|
| `x86_64-linux-full` | `libva.so.2`, `libva-drm.so.2`, `libdrm.so.2`, `libvpl.so.2`, `libasound.so.2` | `libva2 libva-drm2 libdrm2 libvpl2 libasound2t64` |
| `aarch64-linux-full` | `libva.so.2`, `libva-drm.so.2`, `libdrm.so.2`, `libasound.so.2` | `libva2 libva-drm2 libdrm2 libasound2t64` |
| `aarch64-linux-rockchip` | `librockchip_mpp.so.1`, `librga.so.2`, `libdrm.so.2`, `libasound.so.2` | `libdrm2 libasound2t64`, plus the Rockchip BSP's MPP and RGA libraries |

Every artefact also links `libssl.so.3` (package `libssl3t64`), which a standard install already has. On x86_64, `libvpl2` is needed on every host, Intel or not.

Hardware backends need their drivers as well. Without them the edge starts normally and runs on CPU:

- **NVENC / NVDEC**: the NVIDIA driver. Under the packaged systemd unit, `/dev/nvidia-uvm` must also exist before the edge starts (`systemctl enable --now nvidia-persistenced`, or load `nvidia_uvm` at boot): the unit's `NoNewPrivileges=true` stops the driver creating it on first use.
- **VAAPI**: a driver behind `libva2` — `mesa-va-drivers` for AMD (radeonsi), `intel-media-va-driver` (iHD) for modern Intel. The service user must be in the `render` group to open `/dev/dri/renderD*`.
- **QSV** (x86_64): `libmfx-gen1.2`, the Intel GPU runtime that does the encoding and the package most often missing, plus `intel-media-va-driver-non-free` or `intel-media-va-driver`.
- **RKMPP / RGA** (Rockchip): a Rockchip BSP kernel exposing `/dev/mpp_service` and `/dev/rga`, with the service user in the `video` group. The packaged systemd unit already allows both devices; a custom unit needs `DeviceAllow=/dev/mpp_service rwm` and `DeviceAllow=/dev/rga rwm`.
{{SDI_RUNTIME}}

`install-edge.sh` installs the libraries in the table and, for the `-full` artefacts, `va-driver-all` plus `intel-media-va-driver` on x86_64. It does **not** install `libmfx-gen1.2` or the NVIDIA driver, and `va-driver-all` does not bring in the AMD driver on every release, so install `mesa-va-drivers` yourself on AMD. It adds the service user to the `video`, `render` and `audio` groups.

## Verify checksums
```bash
sha256sum -c *.sha256
```

bilbycast-edge is dual-licensed: AGPL-3.0-or-later for open-source use, commercial licence from Softside Tech Pty Ltd for OEM / SaaS / closed-source integration. See `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.commercial`, and the `NOTICE` file inside each tarball.

**Commercial-licence customers**: the Softside commercial licence covers bilbycast source only — it does not relicense libx264 / libx265, which remain GPL-2.0-or-later inside the binary. To avoid GPL copyleft entirely, build from source with `video-encoder-nvenc` only. See `LICENSE.commercial` for the scope statement.

**Patent notice**: H.264 / H.265 patent licensing (MPEG-LA, Access Advance, Velos Media) is separate from software copyright and is the operator's responsibility in commercial deployments. See `NOTICE` in the tarball.

## Remote upgrade

This release is signed for keyless verification by the edge's auto-upgrade pipeline. Operators using the manager UI's `Upgrade` button consume `manifest.json` + `manifest.sig.bundle` automatically. To verify a release manually:
```bash
cosign verify-blob \
    --bundle manifest.sig.bundle \
    --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github\.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/\.github/workflows/nightly-release\.yml@refs/tags/v' \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
    manifest.json
```
See [docs/upgrade.md](https://github.com/Bilbycast/bilbycast-edge/blob/main/docs/upgrade.md) for the full trust model.
